tasks.title: Scaffold Zulip platform plugin metadata
tasks.description: Create the Zulip platform plugin directory and metadata so Hermes can discover the adapter without core source changes.
tasks.details: The current checkout only contains README.md and has no existing plugins/, gateway/, or tests/ tree, so create the upstream-shaped plugin path expected by Hermes: plugins/platforms/zulip/plugin.yaml. Follow the lowercase plugin.yaml convention called out in the PRD unless the target Hermes checkout later shows a different convention. Define name: zulip-platform, label: Zulip, kind: platform, version: 1.0.0, description, and author. Add rich requires_env entries for ZULIP_SITE_URL, ZULIP_BOT_EMAIL, and ZULIP_API_KEY, marking only ZULIP_API_KEY as password: true. Add rich optional_env entries for ZULIP_ALLOWED_EMAILS, ZULIP_ALLOWED_USER_IDS, ZULIP_HOME_EMAIL, ZULIP_HOME_USER_ID, and ZULIP_MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS. Do not add config-file credential fields, stream allowlists, admin lists, webhook configuration, user-account mode, attachment/media settings, or any core Hermes platform enum/runtime entries. Keep the metadata compatible with Hermes plugin discovery described in the platform adapter guide, where requires_env and optional_env are surfaced by hermes config.
tasks.testStrategy: Validate plugin.yaml parses as YAML and contains only the required and optional env vars from the PRD. Add or run a plugin metadata test that loads plugins/platforms/zulip/plugin.yaml and asserts kind == platform, label == Zulip, required credential env vars are present, allowlist vars are optional, and no unsupported webhook/config-file/media vars are exposed.

tasks.title: Implement Zulip adapter configuration and registration hooks
tasks.description: Create adapter.py with environment parsing, validation helpers, env enablement, and Hermes platform registration for Zulip.
tasks.details: Create plugins/platforms/zulip/adapter.py and import the exact APIs from gateway.platforms.base and gateway.config in the target Hermes checkout: BasePlatformAdapter, MessageEvent, MessageType, SendResult, build_source if present, Platform, and PlatformConfig. Implement ZulipAdapter.__init__(config) to read credentials and options from os.environ first and config.extra second: site_url normalized with rstrip('/'), bot_email, api_key, allowed_emails as a lowercase set, allowed_user_ids as a string set, home target from ZULIP_HOME_EMAIL or ZULIP_HOME_USER_ID, and max message chars from ZULIP_MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS when valid. Implement check_requirements() so it returns true only when ZULIP_SITE_URL, ZULIP_BOT_EMAIL, and ZULIP_API_KEY are non-empty and import httpx succeeds. Implement validate_config(config) to validate only base credentials from env/config.extra, not allowlists. Implement _env_enablement() to return None unless base credentials exist, then seed site_url, bot_email, api_key, allowed_emails, allowed_user_ids, max_message_chars, and a home_channel dict with canonical chat_id dm_email:<email> or dm_user:<id> when a home target is configured. Implement register(ctx) with ctx.register_platform(name='zulip', label='Zulip', adapter_factory=lambda cfg: ZulipAdapter(cfg), check_fn=check_requirements, validate_config=validate_config, required_env=['ZULIP_SITE_URL', 'ZULIP_BOT_EMAIL', 'ZULIP_API_KEY'], env_enablement_fn=_env_enablement, cron_deliver_env_var='ZULIP_HOME_EMAIL', allowed_users_env='ZULIP_ALLOWED_EMAILS', max_message_length=8000, platform_hint for Zulip Markdown/current topic behavior, emoji='💬' or an ASCII fallback if the target codebase avoids emoji, and standalone_sender_fn if implemented in the sending task. Keep missing allowlist as an inbound fail-closed condition rather than a config validation failure.
tasks.testStrategy: Use pytest with monkeypatch to cover check_requirements false without base credentials, true with base credentials and importable httpx, validate_config accepting credentials while ignoring missing allowlist, and _env_enablement returning expected extras and home_channel values for email and user-id home targets. Add a fake registry context and assert register(ctx) calls register_platform once with name zulip and the required hooks and metadata.

tasks.title: Implement Zulip HTTP client lifecycle and event queue polling
tasks.description: Add connect, disconnect, queue registration, and long-poll event handling using direct httpx HTTP calls.
tasks.details: In ZulipAdapter, implement direct HTTP using httpx.AsyncClient with Basic Auth username=ZULIP_BOT_EMAIL and password=ZULIP_API_KEY; do not use the official zulip Python package or ~/.zuliprc. Build api_base as f'{site_url}/api/v1'. connect() should validate base credentials, create the AsyncClient, POST /register with data or params encoding event_types=['message'] and apply_markdown=false so raw Markdown is preferred, store queue_id, last_event_id, event_queue_longpoll_timeout_seconds, max_message_length when returned, and any bot identity fields available in the register response. Start a background asyncio polling task only after successful registration, then call self._mark_connected() and return True. If both allowlist sets are empty, log a warning that inbound Zulip messages will be rejected. disconnect() should signal the poll loop to stop, cancel and await the polling task, close the AsyncClient, optionally delete the queue only if a trivial supported endpoint exists in the target checkout, and call self._mark_disconnected(). Implement _poll_loop() to GET /events with queue_id and last_event_id, long-poll timeout, process only event type message, ignore heartbeat/non-message payloads, update last_event_id to the highest event id seen during this process, and continue after modest sleeps on network/API errors. If Zulip returns result='error' with code='BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID', log queue expiry, call the same queue registration helper again, and continue fresh without fetching backlog or persisting event IDs. The current Zulip docs recommend filtering register queues to event_types=['message'], expose last_event_id for GET /events, and require reinitialization on BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID.
tasks.testStrategy: Mock httpx.AsyncClient with async post/get/aclose methods. Verify connect posts to /api/v1/register with event_types ['message'], stores queue_id/last_event_id/max_message_length, starts a poll task, and marks connected only after registration succeeds. Test registration failure returns False or raises according to BasePlatformAdapter patterns without marking connected. Test poll loop ignores heartbeat/non-message events, advances last_event_id, handles BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID by calling the register helper again, sleeps and continues on httpx errors, and disconnect cancels the task and closes the client.

tasks.title: Implement inbound authorization, invocation, and MessageEvent routing
tasks.description: Convert allowed Zulip DMs and invoked stream/topic messages into Hermes MessageEvent objects while rejecting unauthorized or unsupported input.
tasks.details: Add inbound helpers in plugins/platforms/zulip/adapter.py: _is_authorized(message) should match lowercased sender_email against allowed_emails or str(sender_id) against allowed_user_ids, and return false when both allowlists are empty. For unauthorized DMs, call send() with a short denial such as 'You are not authorized to use this Hermes bot.'; for unauthorized streams, silently ignore and log minimal metadata without content. Add _is_self_message(message) comparing sender_email to bot_email and sender_id to any bot user id discovered during register. Ignore reactions, message edits, deletes, and other update events based on event/message operation fields present in Zulip payloads. Accept DMs/private/direct messages from allowed users, including bare slash commands. For stream messages, accept only when the bot is mentioned or when direct-reply-to-Hermes detection is feasible from event metadata without fetching history; bare stream slash commands must be ignored. Mention detection should use message flags when Zulip supplies mention flags and also tolerate common Zulip Markdown mention syntax such as @**Bot Name** without hardcoding a specific display name; derive names from register state, bot_email local part, sender metadata, or config. Strip a leading bot mention from forwarded stream content when practical. Build stable chat IDs using helpers such as dm:<recipient_id_or_sorted_ids> and stream:<stream_id_or_encoded_name>:topic:<url_encoded_topic>, using urllib.parse.quote for reversible safe topic encoding. Build MessageEvent using the exact BasePlatformAdapter API in gateway/platforms/base.py, include MessageType.TEXT or the appropriate enum, source metadata with platform='zulip', chat_id, chat_name, chat_type, user_id, user_name, and metadata fields for Zulip message id, sender email/id/name, stream id/name, topic, recipient_id, and permalink if available. Call await self.handle_message(event) exactly once per accepted inbound message.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test pure helpers and routing with a fake adapter whose handle_message records events. Cover fail-closed missing allowlist, case-insensitive email allowlist, user-id allowlist, unauthorized DM denial via mocked send, unauthorized stream ignore, bot self-message ignore by email and user id, DM message accepted, DM slash command accepted, stream without mention ignored, stream with mention accepted with leading mention stripped, stream slash command without mention ignored, stream slash command with mention accepted, reaction/edit/delete ignored, stable chat IDs for same stream/topic and different chat IDs for different topics, safe encoding of spaces/slashes/colons/Unicode in topics, and metadata presence on produced MessageEvent objects.

tasks.title: Implement Zulip outbound send and home delivery
tasks.description: Send Hermes replies back to the same Zulip DM or stream/topic, including long-message splitting and clear failure results.
tasks.details: Implement ZulipAdapter.send(chat_id, content, reply_to=None, metadata=None) to route by metadata first and canonical chat_id second. For stream replies, POST /api/v1/messages with type='stream', to=<stream name or id>, topic=<topic>, content=<markdown>. For DMs, POST with type='direct', to=[<user_id>] for dm_user:<id> or [<email>] for dm_email:<email>/email targets, and content=<markdown>; use direct rather than private. Home delivery must be DM only and use ZULIP_HOME_EMAIL or ZULIP_HOME_USER_ID seeded in home_channel. Add _split_message(content, limit) where limit is ZULIP_MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS if configured, else max_message_length from /register, else 8000. Split on blank-line/paragraph boundaries first, preserve fenced code blocks where practical by avoiding splits inside triple-backtick spans unless a single block exceeds the limit, hard split oversized blocks, and send chunks sequentially to the same conversation without noisy part prefixes. If any chunk send fails because httpx raises or Zulip returns result != success, log a normal error without API keys or full message bodies and return SendResult(success=False, error=<short reason>) for the overall send; do not enqueue retries or pretend success. Return SendResult(success=True, message_id=<last Zulip id if available>) only when every chunk succeeds. If straightforward after send() exists, implement _standalone_send(pconfig, chat_id, message, **kwargs) by constructing a temporary ZulipAdapter or shared stateless HTTP helper, sending to the configured DM, closing the ephemeral client, and returning the dict shape Hermes expects for standalone sender functions.
tasks.testStrategy: Mock the HTTP client and verify stream sends post type stream, to, topic, and content to /api/v1/messages; DM sends post type direct with a one-element list target; home_channel chat IDs dm_email:<email> and dm_user:<id> route correctly. Test long content splits into multiple sequential posts under the configured limit, prefers paragraph boundaries, hard-splits an oversized paragraph, and does not add part prefixes. Test an httpx exception or Zulip error response returns SendResult(success=False, error=...) and stops or reports overall failure without a retry queue. Test standalone sender if implemented by monkeypatching env/config and asserting it performs one ephemeral send and closes its client.

tasks.title: Add mocked unit test suite for Zulip plugin
tasks.description: Create pytest coverage for configuration, registration, lifecycle, inbound routing, chat mapping, sending, and failure behavior without live Zulip credentials.
tasks.details: Because this checkout currently lacks tests/, create tests/plugins/platforms/test_zulip_adapter.py unless the target Hermes checkout has a more specific plugin adapter test location. Use pytest and pytest-asyncio if already present in the target project; otherwise follow the repository's existing async test convention. Keep all tests mocked and never require a live Zulip server, real API key, ~/.hermes, or ~/.zuliprc. Provide fixtures for PlatformConfig-compatible objects, fake httpx responses, fake AsyncClient, and an adapter subclass or monkeypatch that records _mark_connected/_mark_disconnected/handle_message/send calls. Cover the minimum PRD matrix: config/env checks, _env_enablement seeding, fail-closed missing allowlist, email and user-id authorization, connect queue registration, poll task lifecycle, BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID re-register behavior, heartbeat/non-message ignores, DM routing, stream mention routing, slash-command rules, self-message ignore, reactions/edits/deletes ignored, unauthorized DM denial, unauthorized stream silence, chat ID stability and safe encoding, send payloads for stream and DM, long-message splitting, send API failure, plugin register(ctx) hooks, plugin metadata env vars, and platform_hint. Avoid brittle assertions on raw log text except ensuring sensitive values such as API keys and message bodies are absent if log capture is used.
tasks.testStrategy: Run focused tests with pytest for the new file, for example `pytest tests/plugins/platforms/test_zulip_adapter.py`. If the target Hermes checkout has registry/plugin tests, also run the nearest plugin discovery or platform registry test file to ensure plugin.yaml and register(ctx) are compatible. Confirm the test suite passes with no Zulip-related environment variables set except those explicitly monkeypatched inside individual tests.

tasks.title: Document Zulip plugin setup and v1 limitations
tasks.description: Add concise plugin documentation covering environment setup, behavior, testing, and explicitly unsupported v1 features.
tasks.details: Create plugins/platforms/zulip/README.md. Document installation as a Hermes platform plugin, with both checkout path plugins/platforms/zulip/ and runtime-local ~/.hermes/plugins/zulip/ deployment if relevant. List required env vars ZULIP_SITE_URL, ZULIP_BOT_EMAIL, ZULIP_API_KEY, and either ZULIP_ALLOWED_EMAILS or ZULIP_ALLOWED_USER_IDS, emphasizing fail-closed behavior when both allowlists are missing. List optional ZULIP_HOME_EMAIL, ZULIP_HOME_USER_ID, and ZULIP_MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS. Describe behavior: Zulip bot account only, Events API polling, allowed DMs accepted, stream/topic messages accepted only on bot mention or supported direct replies, stream+topic maps to separate Hermes conversations, Markdown text only, long replies split in-place, no backlog replay after restart, and home delivery is DM-only. Explicitly state v1 exclusions from the PRD: no webhook mode, user-account mode, workspace-wide ingestion, stream allowlists, admin lists, attachments/media, typing indicators, durable outbound queue, edit/delete sync, reaction triggers, or live integration tests. Include the exact focused pytest command for mocked tests. Do not include real secrets or Andy-specific IDs/domains.
tasks.testStrategy: Review README.md for accuracy against plugin.yaml and adapter.py env var names. Run a grep or scripted check to ensure no placeholder real-looking API keys, hardcoded personal emails/domains, or unsupported configuration names were introduced. If documentation linting exists in the target Hermes checkout, run the relevant markdown or docs check.
